newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate edges down on auction, firm peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate edges down on auction, firm peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down five basis points at 23.15 percent on Wednesday, with primary rate hikes offsetting the effect of a stronger peso, traders said.
"The increase in primary (Cetes) rates kept secondary rates up," a money market analyst said.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 22.33 percent at Tuesday evening's primary auction, a rise of 47 basis points from last week.
Money market traders surveyed prior to the auction by Reuters had forecast an average increase of 80 basis points.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 0.7 of a centavo firmer at 7.8930/7.8970 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper were unchanged at 25.00 percent.
The analyst said that ample market liquidity and a favorable outlook for March inflation figures could keep secondary rates on a downward trend.
"The central bank has been draining money every day which means there is cash in the system, it is liquid and recent increases (in rates) have been due to speculation," he added.
Banco de Mexico is expected to release inflation data for March shortly before the close of trade on the money market.
Mexico City financial houses surveyed by Reuters MXAAP forecast an average increase of 1.31 percent in consumer prices for March, compared to 1.68 percent in February.
Liquidity of 1.903 billion pesos was programmed to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
